newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW - Techs stealing the limelight, for now.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - Techs stealing the limelight, for now.

text.p: Spirits are running high in the initial public offering market. Small stocks have surged over the past three weeks, deals have picked up surprising gains and a rosy second quarter seems in store.

Nowhere is hope running higher than the technology sector. But investors should be warned that though spirits and buzz surrounding Internet IPOs are running high, long-term gains in stock prices do not necessarily follow.
"We are talking about stocks walking around on a pair of bamboo stilts here though," said David Menlow, president of the IPO Aftermarket.

Optimism whipped up the openings of two recent tech IPOs, Rambus Inc. and Internet bookseller Amazon.Com Inc. earlier this month. Wall Street is already talking about high speed Internet access provider AtHome Corp., which has filed to go public and is being pitched as the heir to the legacy of market leader Netscape Communications Corp..
"They have gotten rid of that shrould of ugliness," Menlow said, which descended last summer on small-cap technology IPOs. Small stocks, including new issues, also suffered in the first quarter.
Indeed, Netscape's legacy is a mixed one. That stock, which surged as high as $87 amid great fanfare, is now trading only slightly higher than its market debut price.

But portfolio managers are not likely to forget the black eyes they got during the slumps in the small stocks market and are may be more tempted to take quick profits and "flip" shares, analysts said.

An overall pickup in demand for new issues is adding to the possibility for sky-high premiums for tech stocks. After many institutional investors virtually ignored the IPO market in the first quarter, underwriters have priced companies at reasonable valuations and supply is moderate, analysts say.

Glee ensued when the Nasdaq toppled its January record and surged to a new high of 1,389.72 ahead of the Memorial Day weekend. A key index of small stocks, the Russell 2000, gained 4.21 points to a new high of 375.67.

But investors must be wary about investing in start-up firms and even more so when prices are rocketing. Amazon, which surged 66 percent to a high of 30 on their first day fell last week to 15-3/4, below an IPO price of $18.
"The piranhas bit in....The moral is: be careful where you swim," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.

The shortened holiday week ahead should put a slight damper on the volume of IPOs, analysts say. Cary International Inc. CARY.O could be one of the hottest deals of the week with premiums of $2 to $3, according to Fitzgibbon.

The Washington, D.C. company's strategy is to consolidate the highly fragmented vehicle chauffering industry, according to its prospectus. It plans to offer 2.9 million shares for $10 to $12 apiece in an offering via Montgomery Securities. The range had previously been $11 to $13. Carey owns operations but also licenses its name. It has affiliates in 420 cities in 65 countries.

Also going public is Irish airline Ryanair Holding Ltd. and Alexandria Real Estate Equities Inc. ARE.N, a real estate investment trust (REIT) offering 6.75 million shares at $20 to $22. REITs, which own real estate properties, tend to have large market capitalizations and offerings.
"They just suck some of the life and the money out of the marketplace, they're so big," said Menlow.
With summer closing in, invesment bankers are speeding up some their schedules and bringing deals earlier than expected before Wall Street starts taking vacations.

Lary Aasheim, vice president at CoreStates Investment Advisers Inc., said IPOs "are catching a streak before the summer. P/E's (price earnings ratios) tend to contract over the summer and companies want to get the best price," he said.

Last week, several IPOs posted strong performances. LHS Group Inc., which provides billing software to the wireless industry, almost doubled after its debut last week. According to MCM CorporateWatch, eight IPOs went public last week raising $1.83 billion.
